title: Predictable Defender Holidays and Interstate Attack Attempts: A Conditional Theory Test
research_question: Are attacker-identified interstate military attack attempts more frequent on predictable holidays of the defending country, conditional on conflict risk set and observable seasonality?
mechanism: Candidate inspection game: if defender readiness has a larger holiday-specific cost, mixed-equilibrium attack frequency rises; this is conditional, not a general holiday effect and not a proven causal design.

hypotheses.prediction: When holidays raise defenders' readiness costs while other incentives remain fixed, attack attempts become more likely.

study_limitations: DRAFT. No directed interstate dyad-day panel has yet been assembled or validated. Defender holiday is NOT a direct observation of readiness cost. Attack attempts require independently verified attacker/defender direction and no-event risk days. Association only; no causality or novelty established. Not a DiD or RDD. Original articles require full-text reading.
